samples.summary: New `.catch(() => {})` swallows font-fetch failures, and the claimed downstream detection does not exist
samples.evidence: `document.fonts.load(...).catch(() => {})` (line 374) now swallows every rejection. The adjacent comment asserts "a rejection here means the fetch failed, which the check pass below reports as a timeout naming the family", but `document.fonts.check()` (line 388) returns true whenever no registered FontFace matches the query (CSS fallback semantics) and for faces whose status has settled to `error`. So if fonts.googleapis.com is unreachable/blocked in CI — the very scenario the todo doc (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:52-55) claims is now loudly reported — `check()` passes trivially, the catch-all poll at line 395 also passes (`status` is `error`/`unloaded`, not `loading`), and the harness silently screenshots fallback glyphs. Before this change the rejection propagated out of `page.evaluate` and failed the run loudly.

samples.summary: Catch-all "no face loading" poll is trivially satisfiable and misses failed/never-started faces
samples.evidence: `[...document.fonts].every((face) => face.status !== "loading")` returns true for faces in `unloaded` (fetch not yet started, e.g. text laid out a tick later) and `error` (fetch failed). `waitForFunction` polls until the predicate is TRUE, so the very first poll can succeed before any pending fetch transitions to `loading`, making the guard a no-op in exactly the race it is meant to close.

samples.summary: Missing `document.fonts` guard in the two waitForFunction predicates (present in loadPass)
samples.evidence: `loadPass` guards with `if (!document.fonts) return;` (line 367), but the polled predicates at lines 388 and 395 dereference `document.fonts` unguarded. In an environment without FontFaceSet these throw a TypeError inside the page, which Playwright surfaces as an evaluation failure rather than the intended skip — the guard's intent is bypassed on the same code path it protects.

samples.summary: Uniform weight matrix applied to families that do not serve all four weights may hard-fail the 10s check poll
samples.evidence: VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS = [400,500,600,700] is applied to every family, but packages/frontend/index.html:12 requests `Fraunces:...500;600;700` (no 400) and `JetBrains Mono:wght@400;500` (no 600/700). Correctness depends entirely on CSS weight-matching falling back to a neighbouring face inside the FontFaceSet; if any browser/font-loading path returns false for the unserved weight, the new `waitForFunction(..., {timeout: 10000})` at line 384-393 hard-fails the whole visual lane instead of capturing.

samples.summary: `page.evaluate` awaiting `document.fonts.ready` has no timeout — can hang the lane indefinitely
samples.evidence: Both `await page.evaluate(loadPass, spec)` calls (lines 381, 383) await `document.fonts.ready` inside the page. `page.evaluate` is not bounded by the 10s timeouts added below; if a face never settles (offline/hung fetch of the newly-added remote families Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono) the script blocks with no diagnostic instead of failing. The added families increase how much remote loading this unbounded await depends on.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described: verify-visual-browser.mjs:374 swallows every rejection from document.fonts.load() with `.catch(() => {})`, justified by a comment (lines 371-373) claiming "the check pass below reports as a timeout naming the family." That justification does not hold. The check pass is a single page.waitForFunction over all families/weights (lines 384-393), so its failure is a generic Playwright "Timeout exceeded" that names no family; and the catch-all poll (lines 394-398) only rejects `status === "loading"`, so faces settled to `error`/`unloaded` pass it. When fonts.googleapis.com is unreachable no FontFace is registered at all, and `document.fonts.check()` returns true under CSS fallback semantics, so neither wait detects the failure. I could not confirm from the repo whether Blink's check() returns false for error-status faces, which is the one scenario where the swallow might still be caught downstream; that uncertainty keeps the finding rather than refuting it. A concretely reachable harm exists: in updateBaseline mode (lines 533-546) captures are written directly into tests/visual/baselines with no font-liveness assertion, so a swallowed font-fetch failure bakes fallback glyphs into committed baselines. In compare mode the mismatch would still exit 1 (lines 623-628), which makes the reviewer's "silently screenshots fallback glyphs" framing overstated for that path, but that affects magnitude, not whether the swallowed error is real. Swallowed error handling is explicitly inside the correctness lane, so no named refutation ground (not-present, already-guarded, out-of-scope) applies.
